question: A wholesaler marks up the price of a microwave oven by 60% above its cost price. He gives a 15% trade discount to a retailer. The retailer, in turn, marks up the price by 25% above his purchase price and offers a 10% festival discount to the customer. If the customer finally pays ₹14,490 for the microwave, what is the original approximate cost price of the oven to the wholesaler?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In successive chain transactions, the equivalent multiplying factor method is the fastest.

Net multiplying factor = 1.60 (wholesaler markup) × 0.85 (wholesaler discount) × 1.25 (retailer markup) × 0.90 (retailer discount)

Net factor = 1.60 × 0.85 × 1.25 × 0.90 = 1.53

14490 = Original CP × 1.53 ⇒ CP = 14490 ÷ 1.53 ≈ 9470.588

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,471.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Final Selling Price (paid by customer) = ₹14,490

Let the original cost price of the microwave to the wholesaler be 100x.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Wholesaler's Marked Price (MP) = 100x + 60% of 100x = 160x

⇒ Trade discount given by wholesaler = 15% of 160x = 24x

⇒ Retailer's Cost Price (CP) = 160x − 24x = 136x

⇒ Retailer's Marked Price (MP) = 136x + 25% of 136x = 136x + 34x = 170x

⇒ Festival discount given by retailer = 10% of 170x = 17x

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) = 170x − 17x = 153x

⇒ According to the given data, Final SP = 14490

⇒ 153x = 14490

⇒ x = 14490 ÷ 153 ≈ 94.7058

⇒ Wholesaler's Cost Price = 100x = 100 × 94.7058 = 9470.58

⇒ Approximate original cost price = ₹9,471

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,471.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The formula used is: SP = MP × (1 − Discount / 100).

Markup Percentage

Markup is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) before any discount is offered. The formula used is: MP = CP × (1 + Markup / 100).

Successive Transactions

When an article passes through multiple hands where percentage increases or decreases occur consecutively, the Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) × ...
